Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 27-Nov-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  FIRST SEMESTER M.TECH EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  Advanced Computer Architecture [ECE_5421]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                     Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Suppose you are designing a 32-bit RISC ISA with 16 general-purpose registers. You can choose         (5)  
  between: (i) 3-operand instruction format, and (ii) 2-operand instruction format.  
  A)           Compare their impact on:  
  
  Instruction encoding length  
  Datapath complexity  
  Register file read/write ports  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           A datapath includes the following stage delays:                                                       (5)  
  
  Instruction Memory: 250 ps  
  Register File Read: 120 ps  
  ALU: 180 ps  
  Data Memory: 250 ps  
  Register Write: 100 ps  
  
  (i) Compute the critical path delay for a single-cycle CPU.  
  (ii) Discuss how splitting the datapath into multiple cycles or pipeline stages would improve  
  performance.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2)                Differentiate between volatile and non-volatile memories and Explain the difference between ROM, (4)  
  PROM, EPROM, and EEPROM.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  B)           Explain how cache coherence is maintained in multi-core systems.                                      (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  C)           A processor has a 5-stage pipeline: IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB.                                         (4)  
  Given the instruction sequence below, identify any hazards and describe how they can be resolved  
  (with or without stalls):  
  
  1. LW R1, 0(R2)  
  2. ADD R3, R1, R4  
  3. SUB R5, R3, R6  
  
  Page #1

4. SW R5, 8(R2)  
  
  Identify all data hazards (RAW, WAR, WAW) and Indicate which can be resolved by forwarding and  
  which require stalling.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)        What are the main limitations of a single-cycle CPU in terms of clock period and performance?       (2)  
  
  A)                                              Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  B)   Discuss trade-offs in area, power, speed, and control complexity between single-cycle and multi-    (5)  
  cycle CPUs when implemented in VLSI. Include physical design considerations like clock  
  distribution and critical path reduction.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)   Suppose a single-cycle CPU's critical path runs through:                                            (3)  
  Instruction Memory → Register File → ALU → Data Memory → Write Back  
  Propose one architectural modification to reduce the critical path delay. Justify how each change  
  impacts CPI and hardware complexity.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4)        Compare the hardware resource utilization between single-cycle and multi-cycle designs.             (2)  
  
  A)                                              Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  B)   A single-cycle processor has the following component delays:                                        (4)  
  
  $$Instruction Memory = 200 ps$$  
  $$Register File Read = 100 ps$$  
  $$ALU = 150 ps$$  
  $$Data Memory = 250 ps$$  
  $$Register Write = 100 ps$$  
  
  (i) Determine the clock period for a single-cycle CPU.  
  (ii) Suggest how a multi-cycle design can reduce this clock period, and estimate the improvement.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)   Explain how registers, ALUs are shared among cycles in a multi-cycle CPU to reduce hardware         (4)  
  cost. Provide an example showing which hardware blocks are reused.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
5)        Compare direct-mapped, fully associative, and set-associative cache organizations.                  (3)  
  
  
  A)                                              Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  B)   Define memory hierarchy in computer architecture. Explain why it is essential for bridging the      (3)  
  processor-memory speed gap.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  C)   What are the major steps in interrupt handling in a CPU?                                            (4)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"
